title: ICSE CLASS 2 — Environmental Studies | Government Basics
description: Subject-wise test on Government Basics (Environmental Studies) for ICSE CLASS 2. 25Q.
subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Who helps to make rules for everyone in a country or city?

options.explanation: Friends do not make rules for a country or city.
The government makes rules and decisions for a country or city.
Pets do not make rules for a country or city.
Toys do not make rules for a country or city.

questions.explanation: The government is a group of people who make rules and decisions for a country or city to ensure order and well-being.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Why do we need rules in our school and home?

options.explanation: Rules are not made to make noise.

options.text: To keep us safe and in order
options.explanation: Rules help us to live and work together peacefully, safely, and in an organized manner.
Rules are not made to play all the time.
Rules are not made to make things difficult.

questions.explanation: Rules help us to live and work together peacefully, safely, and in an organized manner.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: What is the main job of a leader in a group or community?

options.explanation: Playing games is not the main job of a leader.
Leaders help make decisions, guide others, and ensure that the group or community functions well.
Sleeping all day is not the main job of a leader.
Making everyone sad is not the main job of a leader.

questions.explanation: Leaders are people who help make decisions, guide others, and ensure that the group or community functions well.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: If there were no traffic rules on the road, what would most likely happen?

options.explanation: Without traffic rules, the roads would be chaotic and dangerous.
Without traffic rules, there would be chaos and danger, leading to many accidents.
Without traffic rules, the roads would not be empty.
Cars cannot fly.

questions.explanation: Traffic rules are made to ensure safety and prevent accidents on the road. Without them, there would be chaos and danger.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Your city needs a new park for children to play. Who usually decides where to build it and how much money to spend?

options.explanation: Children do not decide where to build a park or how much money to spend.
The local government makes decisions about public facilities and services.
Animals do not decide where to build a park or how much money to spend.
A famous singer does not decide where to build a park or how much money to spend.

questions.explanation: The local government is responsible for making decisions about public facilities and services like parks, roads, and schools in a city or town.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to have rules in a community?

options.explanation: Keeping people safe is a good reason to have rules.

options.text: To make sure everyone is treated fairly
options.explanation: Making sure everyone is treated fairly is a good reason to have rules.
Creating confusion and fights is not a good reason to have rules.

options.text: To help people live together peacefully
options.explanation: Helping people live together peacefully is a good reason to have rules.

questions.explanation: Rules are made to prevent confusion and fights, and to promote peace and safety, not to cause problems.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: A group of people who make important decisions and manage a country or city is called the:

options.explanation: A school team does not make important decisions for a country or city.
A family does not make important decisions for a country or city.
The government makes important decisions and manages a country or city.
A sports club does not make important decisions for a country or city.

questions.explanation: The government is the body responsible for governing a state, community, or country by making and enforcing laws.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Imagine a school where no one listens to the teachers, and children do whatever they want. What problem would this cause?

options.explanation: Without rules and guidance, learning would be difficult.

options.text: The school would be very organized
options.explanation: Without rules and guidance, the school would be chaotic.

options.text: There would be a lot of disorder and less learning
options.explanation: Without rules and guidance, the school would become chaotic, making it difficult to learn and maintain order.
Teachers would not be happy in a chaotic school environment.

questions.explanation: Without rules and guidance from teachers (who act as leaders), a school would become chaotic, making it difficult to learn and maintain order.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Read the two statements below: Statement 1: It is important for us to follow rules made by the government. Statement 2: Following rules helps to keep our community safe and orderly. Which of the following is true?

options.explanation: Both statements are true.
Both statements are true.

options.text: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 explains Statement 1
options.explanation: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 provides the reason why Statement 1 is important.
Both statements are true.

questions.explanation: Statement 1 correctly states the importance of following rules, and Statement 2 provides the reason why, making it a correct explanation.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: If your classroom needs a new timetable for games, who would usually help decide it to make sure everyone gets a turn fairly?

options.explanation: The classroom walls do not decide the timetable for games.
The teacher decides the timetable for games to ensure everyone gets a turn fairly.
Your pencil box does not decide the timetable for games.
A flying bird does not decide the timetable for games.

questions.explanation: The teacher acts as a leader in the classroom, making decisions that are fair and beneficial for all students, similar to how a government manages a community.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: What do we need to make sure everyone in our school or community stays safe and gets along well?

options.explanation: More toys do not ensure safety or harmony.
Rules are necessary to maintain safety and order.
Only games do not ensure safety or harmony.
Loud music does not ensure safety or harmony.

questions.explanation: Rules are necessary to maintain safety, order, and harmony among people in any group or community, including schools.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Who is responsible for making sure the roads in our city are well-maintained and clean?

options.explanation: Our parents are not responsible for road maintenance.
Our neighbours are not responsible for road maintenance.
The local government is responsible for road maintenance and cleanliness.
Our friends are not responsible for road maintenance.

questions.explanation: The local government is primarily responsible for public services such as road maintenance and cleanliness.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is a service that the government provides for all citizens?

options.explanation: Private tuition classes are not provided by the government.
Public parks are provided by the government for all citizens.
Personal cars are not provided by the government.
Expensive toys are not provided by the government.

questions.explanation: Public parks are common examples of shared resources and services provided by the government for the recreation and well-being of all citizens.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: A group of people who make important rules and decisions for a country is called the:

options.explanation: The government makes important rules and decisions for a country.
A playgroup is not responsible for making rules and decisions for a country.
A family is not responsible for making rules and decisions for a country.
A sports team is not responsible for making rules and decisions for a country.

questions.explanation: The government is the body of people that governs a country, making laws and decisions for its citizens.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Why is it important for children to follow traffic rules, even when walking on the road?

options.explanation: Following traffic rules does not make cars go faster.
Following traffic rules is not related to learning new games.

options.text: To keep themselves safe from accidents.
options.explanation: Following traffic rules helps keep children safe from accidents.
Following traffic rules does not help others break rules.

questions.explanation: Following traffic rules, even as a pedestrian, is crucial for personal safety and preventing accidents on the road.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Imagine your local park has broken swings and a dirty slide. Who should your parents contact to get these problems fixed?

options.explanation: The principal of your school is not responsible for maintaining public parks.
The local municipal office is responsible for maintaining public parks.
The doctor at the clinic is not responsible for maintaining public parks.
The shopkeeper nearby is not responsible for maintaining public parks.

questions.explanation: The local municipal office or local government body is responsible for maintaining public parks and addressing issues like broken equipment or cleanliness.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these community helpers works to maintain law and order and helps people follow rules in the community?

options.explanation: A teacher is not primarily responsible for maintaining law and order.
A doctor is not primarily responsible for maintaining law and order.
A police officer is responsible for maintaining law and order.
A baker is not primarily responsible for maintaining law and order.

questions.explanation: Police officers are primarily responsible for enforcing laws, maintaining public order, and ensuring people follow rules in a community.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: If there were no rules or government in a society, what would most likely happen?

options.explanation: Without rules, people may not always be happy.
Without rules, people may not get free food.

options.text: There would be confusion and disorder.
options.explanation: Without rules, there would likely be confusion and disorder.
Without rules, not everyone would become a leader.

questions.explanation: Without rules and a governing body, societies tend to experience chaos, confusion, and a lack of order, making it difficult for people to live together peacefully.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Assertion (A): The government helps to build schools and hospitals for everyone. Reason (R): Providing education and healthcare are important duties of a government. Which of the following is true?

options.text: Both A and R are false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true, and R explains A.

questions.explanation: Governments typically invest in public services like schools and hospitals because providing education and healthcare are considered essential responsibilities to ensure the well-being of their citizens.

questions.question: Look at the picture below (imagine a picture showing a clean street with dustbins, streetlights, and a public tap for water). These services are usually provided by:

options.explanation: These services are not provided by private companies only.
These services are not provided by wealthy individuals.

options.text: The local government for the community.
options.explanation: These services are provided by the local government for the community.
These services are not provided by schools for their students.

questions.explanation: Clean streets, streetlights, and public water taps are common examples of public infrastructure and services that are managed and provided by the local government for the benefit of the entire community.

questions.question: What is one important job of the government in our country?

options.explanation: This is not a job of the government.

options.text: To make rules for everyone to follow
options.explanation: The government creates and enforces laws for the well-being of society.
This is a recreational activity, not a government job.
This is not related to government functions.

questions.explanation: A primary function of the government is to create and enforce rules (laws) to ensure order and safety in society.

questions.question: Who is responsible for keeping our country safe from harm and protecting its citizens?

options.explanation: While neighbours can be helpful, they are not primarily responsible for national safety.
Pets are not capable of ensuring national safety.
The government has agencies like the police and armed forces for this purpose.
Toys are inanimate objects and cannot contribute to national safety.

questions.explanation: The government, through its various agencies like the police and armed forces, is responsible for the safety and security of the country and its people.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: If there is a problem like a broken street light or too much garbage on the streets in your city, who should you tell to help solve it?

options.explanation: Shopkeepers are not responsible for civic amenities.

options.text: The local government office (like the Municipality)
options.explanation: These bodies are responsible for maintaining public services and civic amenities.
Friends are not officially responsible for addressing civic issues.
Birds are animals and cannot address civic problems.

questions.explanation: Local government bodies (like a Municipality or Panchayat) are responsible for public services and maintaining civic amenities in cities and towns.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Why is it important for everyone to follow the rules made by the government?

options.text: So that only some people are safe
options.explanation: Rules are meant to ensure safety for all, not just some.

options.text: So that we can have a messy country
options.explanation: Following rules helps maintain order and cleanliness.

options.text: So that everyone can live safely and peacefully
options.explanation: This is the primary reason for having and following rules.

options.text: So that we can break things
options.explanation: Rules are meant to prevent harmful actions, not encourage them.

questions.explanation: Rules are made to ensure order, prevent chaos, and create a safe and peaceful environment where all citizens can live together harmoniously.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: A police officer helps to keep people safe, maintain order, and makes sure rules are followed in our neighbourhood. Which part of our community does a police officer work for?

options.explanation: Toy shops are businesses and not related to law enforcement.
Police officers work for government agencies responsible for law enforcement.
Restaurants are businesses and not related to law enforcement.
Cinema halls are entertainment venues and not related to law enforcement.

questions.explanation: Police officers are part of the law enforcement agencies, which are run by the government to uphold laws and ensure public safety.
